locations.note: Koslov fights for Stalingrad from December 1942, mending phone lines and retaking the railway station, and in January 1943 storms the city hall.
December 1941: Koslov trains with potatoes for grenades and fights in the defence of Moscow.
Davis's Desert Rats raid and hold a desert town, break through the German lines in the Second Battle of El Alamein and push on to El Daba.
January 1943: tank commander David Welsh leads his Crusaders against German armour in north-western Libya.
March 1943: Davis is trapped in a house in Toujane, breaks out in an armoured car and retakes the village the next day.
Davis's unit assaults the German positions in Matmata at the end of March 1943.
June 1944, in the push on Caen: Davis fights through Anctoville and Saint-Louet against Tiger tanks and holds the brigade box at Amayé-sur-Seulles.
D-Day: Taylor's Rangers climb the cliffs of Pointe du Hoc to destroy the German guns and hold the point against counterattacks.
December 1944: Taylor's Rangers take Bergstein, charge the bunkers on Hill 400 and hold the hill against German counterattacks.

routes.name: Pvt. Vasili Koslov
routes.note: From the winter defence of Moscow in 1941 to the street-by-street recapture of Stalingrad and its city hall.

routes.name: Sgt. John Davis
routes.note: With the Desert Rats from El Alamein, with Welsh's tanks across Libya, to Toujane and Matmata in Tunisia, then to the bocage west of Caen.

routes.name: Cpl. Bill Taylor
routes.note: From the cliffs of Pointe du Hoc to Bergstein and Hill 400.
